steps: Note the versions printed by 'python3 -m hwkit env'.
Connect a phone and play music.
Check whether MediaPlayer1 objects appear in the trace with and without bluetoothd --experimental (restart bluetoothd in between).
Open the phone's Bluetooth settings and connect to the Pi.
Start any music app and select the Pi as output.
Mark whether the phone offers the Pi as a speaker.
Connect the phone and start music.
The kit saves 'pw-dump' and 'pactl list short sources' snapshots.
Note the node name and media.class of the phone's audio source.
Play the track bab_startstop_2min on the phone.
The kit records 60 s with the bridge's default command (parec, no fallback).
Run 'hwkit analyze' on the result: decoded blocks, no header, no foreign data.
Connect each phone and play music.
Read the negotiated codec and sample rate (pw-dump / pactl list sources long).
Start the trace, connect the phone, play, pause, disconnect.
Compare the recorded events with the fake-BlueZ expectations (hwkit replay).
Connect the phone and play.
Restart bluetoothd ('sudo systemctl restart bluetooth').
Observe: the bridge releases, re-registers the agent, re-syncs; the phone can reconnect.
Open the pairing window in the WebUI.
Pair the phone with Just-Works (no PIN); check the window closes after 5 minutes.
Repeat with the second phone (Android and iPhone).
Make sure the pairing window is closed.
Try to pair a new phone; it must be refused.
Switch Bluetooth off and on at a paired phone (window closed).
It must reconnect; LMS must not start playing by the connection alone.
Connect phone 1 and play.
Connect phone 2; it must be refused, phone 1 keeps playing.
Remove a paired phone in the WebUI.
Pair it again inside a new pairing window.
While playing: walk out of range / switch Bluetooth off / reboot the phone.
The bridge's stream at LMS must be released at once.
Connect a non-phone device (headset, keyboard).
No stream may start.
Android: start the trace; for each scenario type a marker, perform it, then type 'expect:media' or 'expect:no-media'.
Scenarios: play, pause, resume, track change, seek, app switch, screen lock, quiet passage track, messenger notification, ringtone, navigation prompt, silent video, call.
Afterwards: 'hwkit replay' must report all expectations.
iPhone: same scenarios as C1.
Compare C1/C2 replays; write down which signals separate music from notifications and whether 2 s is enough.
Copy the traces to tests/fixtures/traces/ (anonymised by default).
Android: start the trace, move the phone volume slider in small and big steps.
Note whether MediaTransport1.Volume events arrive and how the LMS volume follows.
iPhone: as D1.
Target a sync group of real players; repeat D1; note per-room levels.
Play bab_continuity_30min on the phone.
The kit records the phone PCM for 30 minutes; analyse drops, repeats, gaps.
Place a USB microphone at the speaker; give its PipeWire source with --mic.
Start the trace and capture; press Play/Pause/Play on the phone 10 times with bab_startstop_2min.
Run 'hwkit latency' on trace + capture.
Leave bab_continuity_30min playing on repeat for 4 hours; capture the last 30 minutes.
While streaming WAV and FLAC: record CPU, RSS, temperature ('hwkit env' + 'top -b -n 60 -d 5').
Pi Zero 2 W on Wi-Fi only: repeat E1 for 30 minutes on a busy 2.4 GHz band.
Pi 3 B+: repeat E1 once on Ethernet, once on Wi-Fi.
Use a real Squeezelite on separate hardware as target; repeat the play/pause/resume steps.
For each real Squeezebox model/firmware: WAV, FLAC, pause, start time, wake from standby, ICY off and on.
Write model and firmware into the device field.
Target a sync group of mixed real players; measure the sync offset with the microphone.
With the owner's consent on the production LMS: switch to a real radio station, then pause/disconnect the phone.
The radio must keep playing; the bridge sends no further commands.
Note the LMS server version; repeat F4's basic play/release check.
Give a guest the device name only. Observe without helping: pair, connect, open their app, press Play, pause, leave.
Write down every point of confusion and the time from Play to sound.
Check the Secure-access page: name service 'avahi'.
On each client open http://hifi-bridge.local:<port>/ (browser) and note whether it resolves.
Compare the fingerprint on the trust page with hifi-status.txt / the console.
Install the CA following the trust page (iPhone, Android).
Open the HTTPS address: lock without warning?
Enable HTTPS-only from that HTTPS session.
iPhone: Share -> Add to Home Screen. Android: menu -> Install app.
Open it from the home screen.
VoiceOver/TalkBack on; go through setup, open the pairing window, read the status.
Note every unnamed control or confusing announcement.
